d29e048b00:
Complex trauma is a phenomenon familiar both from the clinic and from the professional literature. It usually results from prolonged or repeated exposure to traumatic events in childhood - often within significant relationships. Unlike single-incident trauma, it becomes intertwined with central developmental processes and affects the formation of identity, self-image, relationships with others and the experience of the world as a whole.

In these situations we see deep disruption of regulation systems, disconnection between the body and awareness, complex dissociative phenomena, somatization, harm to sexual self-image and functioning, and sometimes also an absence of narrative memory of the trauma - all of which make the processing harder and also shake the therapeutic relationship.

In this course we will offer a clinical and therapeutic roadmap for meeting this challenge. Drawing on extensive experience working with clients who suffer from complex trauma, we have developed an integrated treatment model that uses tools from the psychodynamic approach, from third-wave CBT, and from body and movement work. This combination makes it possible to address emotional and bodily regulation systems, strengthen the capacity for containment, improve relationships and broaden the inner interpretation of stimuli - on the way to a life with a sense of coherence and meaning.

Dissociation is a special mechanism, inherent to trauma, that helps a person in survival mode avoid encountering unbearable horror. Sometimes the situation becomes more complicated and over time creates splits of various kinds, which disrupt and damage everyday life.

Danny Brom will talk about how to identify and how to work with dissociative states.

590eeb07ef: The loss of someone close is a tear in the personal fabric of our lives.
1d5490c1ff:
When a loss occurs in sudden, violent or traumatic circumstances, it is an experience that shakes the psyche and a person's connection with themselves and with others, an experience that creates particular complexity and difficulties in the grieving process.

Led by Nili Lavie, we will spend the day delving into the experience of traumatic grief and its treatment, with the aim of deepening professional understanding and the courage to come into contact with one of the most painful experiences we encounter as therapists and as human beings, and perhaps also to offer an opening for connection and meaning.

Survival mode disconnects us from the parts of the brain responsible for language, so we often meet trauma survivors who find it hard to talk and express themselves in words. Art materials offer a rich, grounded language for expressing the traumatic experience and foster processes of regulation, processing and integration in trauma therapy.

Tamara Weiner will present ways of addressing trauma through art, even when your specialty is not art therapy.

In this course we will learn the basic principles of the ACT (Acceptance and Commitment Therapy) approach and explore ways of integrating them into work with people who have experienced trauma. The course is an introduction offering a first exposure to the approach, focusing on trauma-related avoidance patterns, working with painful emotions, and using values as a central tool for promoting change.

The course is suitable for therapists who want to get to know the ACT approach and expand their tools for working with trauma.

35e4ca1a86:
In extreme situations we see how the components of experience become disconnected from one another, for example emotion disconnecting from functioning, and sometimes components become over-coupled, such as an image or situation that is always accompanied by intense fear.

This process requires trauma therapy to address each component of experience separately and to allow appropriate connections between them, in order to restore the integrative capacity damaged by the trauma and to distinguish what belongs to the present and what to past events.

In the workshop we will learn tools and techniques for integrating this work with the various modes of experience - senses, images, movements and more - in therapy with trauma survivors.

Sexual trauma is a particularly sensitive and complex subject. Beyond the threat to life it sometimes involves, it also involves a violation of basic trust in other people, and it is usually accompanied by guilt and shame.

Michal Zmora will talk about this complex condition and its treatment.
47704f3722:
Childbirth and "birth stories" usually get the public image of an uplifting, mainly joyful event. Yet despite this, and sometimes precisely because of it, about a third of women who give birth will experience the birth as traumatic.

Together we will learn about treating women after childbirth, and about guiding directions for processing and working with births of all kinds (including working with pregnancy loss and stillbirth). We will look in depth at the different experiences, the meaning of the high numbers, and the various causes and consequences.
53c3a78bd3: Narrative work as part of trauma therapy
c0438d3d50: PhD in bibliotherapy, former head of the bibliotherapy department at David Yellin College, longtime therapist at Metiv
ee1e5f6a42:
Narrative therapy is about expanding the confining stories a person sometimes tells about themselves and about the world.

In cases of trauma and loss, beyond the pain, the suffering and the torment, the sense of identity is also harmed. The person feels weak, helpless, hopeless and sometimes guilty as well. In addition, the traumatic event remains in body and mind as if in tatters, and the memories spread and remain without narrative continuity.

In the course we will learn the principles of narrative therapy and get to know various narrative means through which a person's dignity, identity and story can be restored to them. The course will combine theoretical study, clinical examples and personal experiential exercises. Michal Simchon will present tools for stitching together and expanding the post-traumatic narrative, and for working with the narrative when it is stuck and harmful.

Trauma therapy requires the therapist to have a variety of skills and the ability to apply them flexibly with the particular client in the clinic and their unique situation. The transition from a learning setting to clinical work in the field is not simple, and many therapists find it hard to integrate the new knowledge they have acquired in different clinical situations.

To support therapists' skills and the tailored use of the tools taught in our course, we are opening a day devoted entirely to practicing the skills acquired in the course - psychoeducation, grounding, attention and regulation skills, and integrative connection of the components of experience, including the bodily component.

You are invited to join us in person and remotely for courses on trauma. The program includes courses for thorough, comprehensive learning, advanced courses in trauma therapy, supervision options, and joining Metiv's learning community.

Metiv has been operating as a training center for more than 20 years, training therapists, organizations and professionals from a range of fields. The programs are based on broad clinical knowledge and experience, combined with treatment methods from Israel and around the world. To date, more than 2,000 therapists have been trained. The trainings are also offered online.

## What the 2025 program includes

- **Advanced courses, in-depth study and learning units** - Kaleidoscope units: Narrative Work with Post-Traumatic Stress, "Not by Talk Alone", ACT for Trauma Therapy. Coming soon: Trauma on the Continuum, Moral Injury, Psychedelics and Trauma Therapy, Compassion Fatigue: Its Impact on the Therapist and the Therapist's Role.
- **Short, focused, practical courses** - The Roadmap (June), The Roadmap for public bodies and nonprofits (contact shir@metiv.org), a one-day course: Building a Trauma-Informed Organization.
- **Learning community** - Journal Club: a learning community on trauma research and treatment, free of charge. Individual supervision (NIS 450) and a supervision group.
